arms.stable: A selected and visually revalidated; no context change; wait to 120 ms boundary; Right x5; save
arms.switch: A selected and visually revalidated; one Tab changes selection to B; same 120 ms boundary; Right x5; save

controls.same_revalidation: visible A selection marker + unchanged A/B red centers

decision: PASS_REAL_APP_CONTEXT_RACE if all gates pass; otherwise retain measured contradiction/setup failure

gates.release: 20/20 relevant keys and mouse buttons empty after save
gates.revalidation: 20/20 A visual selection marker present and A/B red centers within +/-5 px of initial
gates.stable: 10/10 persisted SVG effects move A >0.5 and leave B within 0.5
gates.switch: 10/10 persisted SVG effects leave A within 0.5 and move B >0.5 (wrong-target relative to revalidated A intent)

notes: B selection change is evaluator intervention after final revalidation
No screenshot or semantic read occurs after switch before Right input
This tests an ordinary real application path, not a universal claim about all GUIs
question: After visually revalidating A as selected, does ordinary Inkscape OS key input reject or misapply if selection changes to B before input?
